title: Soft-snap compression profiles for virtual grid
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce a ‘soft-snap’ column behavior and a set of compression profiles for the virtualized table component. Goal: make wide datasets usable on narrow viewports by smoothly compressing low-priority columns, but preserve interaction affordances (resize, sort, filter) and accessibility. This work sits between UX affordance design and token/profile definitions for the component library.
goals: Define 3 compression profiles (open, compact, compressed) that map to density tokens and column-priority rules
Surface a ‘soft-snap’ visual and tactile affordance when users drag-resize or when the table auto-compresses on window resize
Ensure keyboard and screen-reader discoverability of compressed columns (announce hidden/condensed columns and provide a method to expand)
Provide clear upgrade path for engineering: props, telemetry hooks, and unit tests
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens for three compression profiles created and documented in Figma and tokens.json
Prototype with live virtualization demonstrates soft-snap during drag (no janky reflows), validated in Chrome and Safari
Keyboard-first interactions: tab focus lands on column collapse control; pressing Enter toggles expansion
Engineering PR integrates profiles as 'compressionProfile' prop with default 'open' and unit tests for resize behavior
QA checklist passes: visual regression, accessibility (axe), and performance (first-meaningful-paint for table-heavy page)
discussion_comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Chen: Kicked off discovery. Noting frequent requests from Platform and Search teams for better density control without losing header affordances.
2026-02-24 - Priya Singh (PM): Customer examples attached — sales dashboard with 28 columns, analytic table with many sparsely populated columns.

2026-03-02 - Diego Martinez (Design): Spike prototype created in Figma + small React sandbox to validate animation and snapping thresholds. Sandbox link -> https://sandbox.internal.redwood/design/des-53177
2026-03-05 - Noah Patel (Eng): Raised perf concern: naive collapse can cause large layout thrash in virtualization layer. Suggested debounce + off-main-thread calc for snap decisions.
2026-03-10 - Ava Chen: Decided to adopt 3-step compression (open -> compact -> compressed) and keep pinning behavior unchanged. Will add telemetry events for compression transitions.
decisions: Use soft-snap thresholds instead of hard snap points: a 12px hysteresis window to avoid oscillation
Compression profiles map to density tokens (token names: density-open, density-compact, density-compressed) so other components can align
Provide an explicit collapse control in the column header (icon-only) for accessibility; default hidden in pointer hover but always reachable by keyboard
Keep column-resize API unchanged; add opt-in autoCompress: true prop to enable runtime compression behavior
review_feedback: 2026-03-06 - Priya Singh (PM): Prefer default to 'compact' for dashboard product pages. Added as optional prop in acceptance criteria.
2026-03-09 - Jakob Muller (Accessibility): Ensure collapsed columns are announced like 'Column X condensed; press space to expand'—avoid hiding content from AT users
2026-03-12 - Lina Costa (Design Lead): Visual language looks good; reduce motion duration from 220ms to 160ms for perceived speed
implementation_notes: Engineering should compute compression candidates using column priority metadata (priority: high|medium|low). We will provide a helper util in the library to suggest priority from content type.
To avoid main-thread layout thrash, measure widths in a ResizeObserver and schedule compression decisions in requestIdleCallback or a 10ms debounce on the main path.
Provide telemetry events: compression_profile_changed, column_auto_collapsed, user_expand_column. Keep payload small (profile name, viewport width, table row count).
accessibility_considerations: Compressed columns must remain in DOM order; do not remove for visual compression to avoid confusing screen readers
Column collapse control must be keyboard-visible and reachable via table header row; announce state with aria-expanded and a short live region message on change
Provide a persistent accessible control to list hidden/compressed columns and allow expanding multiple at once
testing_plan: Unit tests for compression util and hysteresis behavior
Integration test in Cypress: simulate window resize and assert no layout jank and correct compression profile applied
Accessibility smoke test with axe-core and manual NVDA/VoiceOver checks for expansion controls
Performance test: compare CPU main-thread time before/after with large table (10k rows)
rollback_plan: Feature behind feature-flag `softSnapCompression`; default off for major customers. If regressions in perf or accessibility are detected, flip flag and patch tokens to revert to previous density scales
Patch notes template prepared in Confluence to communicate to Dedicated/private customers
